terms.label: Basics & Process
terms.description: Powder coating basics start here. These guides explain what powder coating is, how the process works from pretreatment through cure, and what it can and cannot do. They are written for buyers, engineers and owners who are new to the finish and want plain answers before specifying it. You will find a step-by-step walk through the process, the benefits compared with other finishes, the myths we hear most often, how the process affects the environment, and how small parts are handled differently from large fabrications. Start with the definition if powder coating is new to you, then follow the links into the rest of the guides for materials, finishes, standards and cost.

terms.label: Materials & Substrates
terms.description: This powder coating materials guide covers the two things every job starts with: the metal being coated and the powder going onto it. Different substrates behave differently in pretreatment and in the oven, and each powder chemistry has its own strengths. These articles explain which metals can be powder coated, how steel, aluminum, stainless and cast parts are prepared, and how epoxy, polyester and hybrid powders compare for corrosion protection and UV resistance. Use them when you are deciding whether a part is a good candidate for powder coating or choosing a powder for a particular environment.

terms.label: Finishes & Colours
terms.description: Our powder coating finishes guide explains how colour, gloss and texture are specified and what to expect from each option. Colour is usually communicated with a RAL number, but gloss level and texture change how a part looks and wears just as much. These articles cover RAL colour matching and custom colour requests, and how matte, gloss, textured and metallic finishes differ in appearance, durability and maintenance. Read them before you choose a finish for a product line, a building or a restoration, so that what you ask for is what comes out of the oven.

terms.label: Standards, Testing & Quality
terms.description: Powder coating standards and testing define how a finish is specified, measured and verified. This section explains the documents and tests you will see on drawings and in supplier requirements: ASTM test methods for adhesion, impact and film thickness, ISO quality systems, surface preparation standards, salt spray testing and corrosion ratings. It also covers how film thickness is specified in mils and how it is measured, and what a quality control inspection looks like on each batch. Use these guides to write a clearer specification or to understand a test report from your coater.

terms.label: Comparisons
terms.description: These powder coating comparisons set the finish side by side with the alternatives buyers most often consider: wet paint, galvanizing and anodizing. Each process protects metal in a different way, at a different cost, and with a different look. The articles compare durability, corrosion protection, appearance, environmental impact and price, and explain when two processes are combined, such as powder coating over galvanized steel. Read them when you are choosing a finish for a new product or questioning whether the finish on an existing specification is still the right one.

terms.label: Applications
terms.description: Powder coating applications cover the parts and products we see most often and what each one needs from its finish. A farm implement, a conveyor frame, a church gate and a patio chair all get powder coated, but they face different conditions and are prepared and specified differently. These guides go through automotive parts, industrial machinery, agricultural equipment, railings and bollards, fences and gates, conveyor and automation frames, robot bases, food-processing equipment, HVAC ductwork, playground equipment and outdoor furniture. Find the article closest to your part to see the preparation, powder choice and common mistakes for that application.

terms.label: Cost & Planning
terms.description: Powder coating cost and planning guides help you budget a job and get parts ready for it. Price depends on the size and number of parts, the preparation they need, the finish chosen and how they are racked and cured, so understanding those factors makes a quote easier to read. This section explains what drives cost, how to prepare parts before dropping them off so no time is lost at receiving, and which questions to ask a coater before you place an order. Read them before requesting a quote and you will get a faster, more accurate answer.

data.intro: Koojo Custom Powder Coating is the powder coating company GTA fabricators, manufacturers, contractors and vehicle owners call when metal parts need a finish that lasts. From our Milton, Ontario shop, we have coated more than 10,000 steel and aluminum items since 2012 for clients across Toronto, Halton and Peel, from small brackets to 6,000 lb frames. Every part is blasted, pretreated, coated, cured and tested under one roof.

body.text: Since 2012 • 10,000+ items coated • Parts up to 6,000 lb • 48-hour turnaround available • Certified by Absolute Bureau of Certification

children.text: What Is Powder Coating?

Powder coating is a dry finishing process. Thermoset powder is sprayed onto clean, grounded metal with an electrostatic gun, then cured in an oven at roughly 180 to 200 °C. The heat melts the powder into one continuous film that is harder and more chip-resistant than most liquid paints, with no solvents released.

As a powder coating company GTA businesses rely on for repeat work, we focus on what decides how long a finish lasts: surface preparation, correct film thickness and a full cure. Our guides on what is powder coating and powder coating vs wet paint go deeper.
Our Powder Coating Services
We handle every stage in house, so you deal with one shop instead of three. View all our powder coating services.
Industrial Powder Coating
Heavy-duty finishes for machinery, structural steel, guards and frames exposed to abrasion, chemicals and weather. Learn about industrial powder coating.
Surface Preparation
Degreasing, phosphate pretreatment and precise masking, plus in-shop and mobile sandblasting services for rust and mill scale. See our powder coating surface preparation.
Custom Colors & Finishes
RAL-matched gloss, matte, textured, metallic, candy and clear finishes, held consistent on every reorder. Browse custom powder coating colours.
Restoration & Recoating
We strip failed paint or powder to bare metal, treat rust and recoat gates, railings, furniture and vintage parts. Read about powder coat stripping and recoating.
Bulk & Commercial Orders
Recurring production runs scheduled around your shipping dates, with matched colour from the first piece to the last. See our commercial powder coating program.
Automotive Powder Coating
Frames, chassis, suspension parts, valve covers and wheels finished to resist heat, chips and road salt. Explore automotive powder coating and rim powder coating.
Architectural Coatings
Railings, fences, gates and window frames coated with AAMA 2604 and 2605 powders for lasting outdoor colour. View architectural powder coating.
Specialty & Custom Projects
Prototypes, one-off fabrications, signage and art pieces that need careful handling. Ask about specialty powder coating.
Industries We Serve

Most of our work comes from businesses that need a finishing partner every week. We coat to your drawings and schedule around your production. That reliability is why we are the powder coating company GTA shops build into their supply chain. See powder coating by industry.
Metal Fabricators
We remove spatter and mill scale from weldments, coat to spec and return them in time for your delivery. Read about powder coating for metal fabricators.
Manufacturers
Conveyor frames, robotic bases and machine guards coated to OEM colour standards. Read about powder coating for manufacturers.
Machine Shops
Precision masking protects threads, bores and mating faces, so parts go straight to assembly. Read about powder coating for machine shops.
Automotive Shops
Restoration shops and custom builders send frames, chassis and wheels for a durable, show-quality finish. See our automotive powder coating service.
Construction Companies
Stairs, columns, bollards and railings coated on your schedule, with site delivery available. Read about powder coating for contractors.
Welding Shops
Finished assemblies are blasted and coated so every weld is sealed against rust before it leaves our shop. See why welders use us as their welding shop finishing partner.
Shop Capabilities

Our cure oven accepts parts up to 23 ft long, 9 ft wide and 9 ft high, and our lifting equipment handles single pieces up to 6,000 lb. Large frames and chassis are coated whole. Every batch is checked for adhesion to ASTM D3359 and dry film thickness to ASTM D7091. Full specifications are on our large part powder coating page.
Our Powder Coating Process
Every order follows the same five steps. Our step-by-step powder coating process guide explains each one in detail.
Quote & Inspect
We review your photos, drawings or parts, then confirm price, colour and ready date in writing.
Strip & Blast
Old coatings, rust and mill scale are removed, leaving a clean, profiled surface the powder can grip.
Pretreat & Mask
Parts are degreased and phosphate-treated, and threads, holes and contact faces are plugged or taped.
Coat & Cure
Powder is applied electrostatically, then cured at about 180 to 200 °C into one hard, continuous film.
Inspect & Hand Over
We test adhesion and thickness, check colour and coverage, then pack parts for pickup or delivery.
Recent Projects

Recent jobs include a conveyor frame for an automotive plant, an automation line frame, a food processing line frame, a robotic base, safety bollards and restored church gates. Each case study lists the metal, preparation, powder, colour and turnaround. Browse our powder coating projects.
Why Choose Koojo
Choosing a powder coating company GTA clients can trust comes down to experience, capacity and proof.
Experience: 14 years in business and more than 10,000 items coated.
One shop, one crew: no subcontracted blasting or curing, so quality stays under our control.
Capacity: an oven and lifting equipment sized for frames up to 6,000 lb.
Certified quality: certified by the Absolute Bureau of Certification, with test reports on request.
On-site option: mobile sandblasting for structures that cannot travel.
Clear quotes: price, colour and ready date in writing before work begins.
Local logistics: pickup and delivery across the Greater Toronto Area.
Powder Coating Services Across the GTA

Koojo is based in Milton, minutes from Highways 401 and 407, within easy reach of Toronto, Halton and Peel. Being a Milton-based powder coating company GTA clients reach quickly means faster pickups and less transit time. We also serve Oakville, Burlington, Mississauga, Halton Hills and Brampton. Drop parts off Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, or book a pickup. See all our powder coating service areas.

Our shop and drop-off point, where local clients can meet the team and see finished work. Visit our powder coating Milton page.

We coat large and heavy parts in one piece for Guelph manufacturers and agricultural equipment owners. Visit our powder coating Guelph page.
Cambridge
We serve Cambridge fabricators and machine shops with production batches and scheduled pickups. Visit our powder coating Cambridge page.
Hamilton
We finish railings, structural steel and equipment for Hamilton construction and industrial clients. Visit our powder coating Hamilton page.

children.text: If you need these details for a supplier form, Koojo Custom Powder Coating can send them in writing with your estimate.
Our Story

Our company history starts in 2012 with one simple aim: give local businesses a powder coating shop that finishes parts properly, answers the phone and hits the date it promised. More than a decade later, that aim still shapes every order at Koojo Custom Powder Coating.

[Owner name] founded the business in Milton [confirm founding story in the owner's words]. Work grew steadily through word of mouth, the way most customers first heard about us, first from fabricators and machine shops nearby, then from larger manufacturers and public clients across the region. The shop has grown with that demand, adding a 23 ft oven for big parts and certifying its quality system with an outside body. What has not changed is the way jobs are handled. Every order is still checked by people who know the work, and customers can still reach someone who knows their parts. That, more than anything, is what people mean when they talk about Koojo.
The People Behind Your Parts

Our team of experienced coaters handles every stage in-house, from blasting and pretreatment to spraying, curing and inspection. Because nothing is passed to another vendor, the person who plans your job can tell you exactly where it stands.
How We Work: Our Company Values

Three company values guide every job: a quality-first approach, close customer focus and a sustainable process. At Koojo Custom Powder Coating they are practical rules, not slogans, and they decide how we prepare, coat and check each part.
Quality first
We use quality powders, prepare every surface properly and test the finish before release. Our checks are set out on the
powder coating quality assurance
page.
Customer focus

We listen first, then confirm colour, prep and timing before work starts, so nothing on your order is left to guesswork. Ask any repeat customer about us and this is usually the first thing they mention.
A sustainable process
Powder coating produces far less waste than many liquid finishes, and overspray can often be collected. We plan loads to make good use of each oven cycle.
What We Do and Who We Serve

Koojo Custom Powder Coating blasts, prepares, coats and cures metal parts for industrial and individual customers alike. That ranges from production runs of frames and guards to a single bike frame, a set of rims or a restored railing brought in by a homeowner.
Our
powder coating services
page lists every service, including industrial work,
custom powder coating colours
and restoration. For finished examples, browse our
powder coating projects
, and for the cities we cover, see our
powder coating service areas
. Whatever the size of the order, Koojo Custom Powder Coating runs it through the same in-house facility and checks.
Our Facility in Milton

Our in-house facility includes blasting, pretreatment, spray booths and a 23 ft curing oven that takes parts up to 6,000 lb. Mobile sandblasting is also available for items too large or awkward to bring to the shop.
Most visitors who ask about Koojo want to see the oven first.
Keeping blasting, coating, curing and inspection under one roof is what lets us offer a 48 hour turnaround on standard work. For full size and weight limits, see

, which explains what fits and how big jobs are planned at Koojo Custom Powder Coating.

Drop-Off and Pickup, Step by Step

Drop-off and pickup follow eight simple steps, from your first call to collecting finished parts. Following them keeps your visit short and makes sure nothing is missed when your parts reach our shop.
Call Ahead
Before you visit, contact Koojo to book a time, especially for long or heavy items.
Prepare and Label Parts
Remove loose debris, label each part and mark any areas that must stay bare.
Plan Your Route
Use the map above for directions to our shop on Steeles Avenue East in Milton.
Arrive During Opening Hours
Bring parts any weekday between 7 AM and 5 PM. Ask about parking and loading when you call.
Receiving Check
When you reach Koojo, we count the parts, note their condition and confirm the finish with you.
Coating and Curing
Standard orders are prepped, coated, cured and inspected within 48 hours.
Ready Notice
We call or email the moment parts are ready, so you can arrange your pickup schedule.
Pickup or Delivery

children.text: Request Your Quote

The quote request form asks only for what we need to price the job properly. Fill in the required fields, attach drawings and photos if you have them, and press send. Every request is read by a person, not an automated system.

Use the photo upload for clear pictures of each side of the part, and add anything unusual in the project details box, such as a tight deadline, a matching colour from an earlier job or parts that arrive in pieces.

children.text: A clear photo saves more time than any other field. It lets us see rust, old paint and welds before we price the work, so your quote for powder coating matches the part that actually arrives.
What to Send for an Accurate Price
Send part measurements, part quantity, the metal, the finish you want and one or two photos. With those five details we can usually price a job straight away, without a follow-up call.

Measure the longest length, the widest point and the height, including anything that sticks out. For the colour, give the colour code if you have one, such as a RAL number, or describe the look you want and we will suggest options. Note any masking requirements, such as threads, mounting faces or contact points that must stay bare. If the part has old paint or rust, mention it, because removal changes the powder coating estimate. For unusual or very heavy items, a sample part or a drawing helps us give a firm figure rather than a range. The more complete your request, the faster and more accurate your quote will be. A complete powder coating quote request rarely needs a second round of questions, and that keeps your job moving.
How Quoting Works, Step by Step

Quoting follows five steps: you send the request, we review it, we send a written estimate, you approve the job, then parts come in for coating. The table shows what happens at each step and how long it usually takes.

children.text: Our quote turnaround depends on how much detail arrives with the request. Complete requests with photos are usually the quickest to price, and we will tell you if anything is missing.

Nothing is booked until you give job approval. Once you accept the powder coating quote, we confirm drop-off or pickup, reserve oven time and send the timeline in writing. If anything about the part changes after approval, tell us and we will update your quote before work begins, so the final invoice always matches what you agreed.
What Affects the Price

Five price factors shape every powder coating quote: the size of the part, the prep it needs, the quantity, the colour and finish, and the amount of masking. Two parts that look alike can cost different amounts for these reasons.

That is why your quote is always written for your exact part. Heavy rust or old coatings add blasting or stripping time. Large items use more oven space, while a batch of matching parts spreads setup across many pieces. Special colours or textures can cost more than stock shades, and detailed masking takes extra labour. For typical price ranges and what drives them, read our guide to

data.title: Large Part Powder Coating
data.intro: Large part powder coating is what our Milton shop is built for: a 23 ft oven, a weight capacity of up to 6,000 lb and in-house blasting under one roof. Since 2012, Koojo Custom Powder Coating has finished more than 10,000 items, from single brackets to heavy fabrications and complete equipment frames.

body.text: By the Koojo Custom Powder Coating production team | Updated 22 October 2026

children.text: This page sets out exactly what fits, how big work moves through the shop and how long it takes, so you can check your part before you send a drawing. Standard orders carry a 48 hour turnaround, and the shop is open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Each limit is stated plainly, with no guesswork.

body.text: 23 ft Oven | Up to 6,000 lb | 48 Hr Turnaround | In-House & Mobile Sandblasting | Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | Google Rating [add live rating]

children.text: Capacity at a Glance

Our capacity at a glance: parts up to 23 ft long and up to 6,000 lb can be blasted, coated and cured in one cycle. The table below gives the limits, and anything near them is best confirmed with a drawing before you book.

content.text: [confirm one figure: 9 ft x 9 ft or 14 ft x 15 ft]
In-house, plus mobile sandblasting for parts too big to move
One-off parts through recurring bulk work

children.text: Few shops in the region publish a weight limit, so it helps to know ours before planning large-part powder coating. Size and weight both matter: a long, light frame may fit easily, while a compact but very heavy casting may need a closer look at loading and racking. Knowing both numbers early saves a wasted trip with large parts.
Will My Part Fit?

Your part will usually fit if it is shorter than 23 ft, inside the oven's width and height, under 6,000 lb, and has somewhere solid to hang or support it. Check those four points first, then send us the part dimensions for a final yes.

Measure the longest length, the widest point and the tallest point, including anything that sticks out. Add the weight if you know it, or the steel size and length so we can estimate it. Long parts such as beams, rails and structural steel members fit lengthwise, so length is rarely the issue for large parts; width, height and hanging points usually decide. If a part is close to a limit, photos of the welds and lifting points help us plan large part powder coating without surprises on delivery day.
Equipment and Process for Big Work

Big parts follow the same steps as small ones, but each step is planned around size and mass: blasting, pretreatment and masking, then electrostatic coating and a full cure in our large curing oven. Planning comes first, because large parts cannot be reworked cheaply.
Blasting

In-house blasting removes mill scale, rust and old coatings so the powder bonds to clean metal, and mobile sandblasting covers items that are too awkward to move. That step matters most in large part powder coating, where a missed patch is hard to fix later. Learn more about our
sandblasting services
Pretreatment and Masking
Chemical pretreatment improves adhesion and corrosion resistance, and masking protects threads, mounting faces and contact points. Our
powder coating surface preparation
page explains each step.
Coating and Curing

Electrostatic spraying wraps powder around big frames and into corners. The 23 ft oven then cures each piece at 180–200 °C, and heavy sections stay in until the metal itself reaches temperature, which is what keeps a consistent finish on powder coating for large parts.
What We Coat at This Size

Typical large parts include equipment frames, conveyor and automation structures, machine bases, structural steel, railings and gates, trailer and vehicle frames, and heavy machinery coating for plant upgrades. Small parts can ride along in the same order.
Our
industrial powder coating
page covers the full service for heavy frames and machinery, and our
powder coating projects

page shows finished examples with specs and photos. Both are good places to see how parts of this size come out, and how the same quality carries from a single beam to a full skid of large parts bound for a new production line.
From One-Off Jobs to Recurring Volume

We handle one-off and repeat orders with the same care. A single oversized frame gets its own planned cycle, while batch coating suits repeat runs of matching parts, and recurring bulk work can be scheduled to suit your production calendar.
Customers with steady volume often book oven time ahead, which keeps large part powder coating on a predictable rhythm. For pricing and account options on volume work, see
commercial powder coating
, which covers recurring orders in detail. Batch work also makes it easier to keep colour matched across large parts made months apart, and recorded colour codes make later reorders simple.
Quality on Every Big Part

Large parts get the same checks as small ones. We measure film thickness to ASTM D7091 across faces, edges and welds, test adhesion to ASTM D3359, and record the results, so a 20 ft frame meets the same standard as a bracket.
Readings are taken where big parts fail first: long welds, outside corners and the lowest edge of the hang.
Our quality system is certified by the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request. The steps are set out on our
powder coating quality assurance
page, which applies to powder coating large parts as well as everyday work.
Timing and Lead Times

Standard orders are turned around in 48 hours from drop-off. Very large, heavy or complex items may need more time for blasting, masking and cure, so we confirm the timeline in writing when you request a quote.

content.text: Depends on prep and cure time
Heavy sections take longer to heat

children.text: Good lead time planning starts with sizes, quantities and your install date. Tell us all three and we will plan large part powder coating around your deadline.

Short answer: if a part is within 23 ft and 6,000 lb, we can almost always coat it. These answers cover limits, measuring and mixed orders, and they are written for this page only, not copied from other pages.

data.intro: Powder coating quality assurance at Koojo Custom Powder Coating is independently certified by the Absolute Bureau of Certification LLC, covering both powder coating and mobile sandblasting. Since 2012 every one of our 10,000-plus coated items has passed through the same checks at our shop at 10874 Steeles Ave E in Milton.

$media.alt: Koojo quality assurance certification marks

body.text: By the Koojo Custom Powder Coating quality team | Reviewed by [Owner name] | Updated 22 October 2026

children.text: This page explains what the certification covers, which checks we run at each stage, how long they take and which documents you can request for supplier approval or an audit. Standard orders, inspection included, carry a 48 hour turnaround. Whether you buy one bracket or a full production run, the same written quality assurance applies, and the records behind it are available to you. That openness means buyers can check our claims for themselves, line by line, before they place a first order. Read on for the certificate details, the checks at every stage, the tests, the documents you can request and the timing of each step.

body.text: Certified by Absolute Bureau of Certification LLC | Third-Party Test Reports on Request | ASTM Test Methods | Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | 48 Hr Turnaround

children.text: Our Certification

Koojo is a certified powder coater: the Absolute Bureau of Certification LLC has certified our quality system for powder coating and mobile sandblasting. That means our methods are documented, followed and checked by an outside body rather than set by us alone.

Buyers use these details for vendor qualification and powder coating QA reviews, so we keep them current and easy to check. If your procurement team needs the certificate on file before a first order, ask when you request a quote and we will send it with your order paperwork. An independent audit gives your team confidence that our quality assurance is more than a promise.
What Our Checks Cover, Stage by Stage

Our powder coating quality assurance runs from the moment parts arrive to the moment they leave. Each stage has its own inspection checkpoints, and the results go into traceable job records tied to your order number.

content.text: Part count, condition, drawing and finish spec
Clean metal, profile, no remaining rust or scale
Clean, dry surface; masking in place
Visual inspection, DFT readings, adhesion, colour and gloss
Results recorded; inspection report on request

children.text: Writing the checks down is what turns good intentions into quality assurance for powder coating that a customer can verify. It also means a repeat order months later is made to the same acceptance criteria as the first. Final checks combine visual inspection under good light, colour verification against the approved code and a gloss check, so every part matches the sample. Cure checks confirm the metal itself reached temperature, not just the oven air.
Tests We Run and What They Show

Three checks are part of every final inspection: film thickness, adhesion and appearance. Each follows a recognised method, so the numbers mean the same thing to your engineers as they do to our team.

content.text: DFT readings on faces, edges, welds

children.text: Readings are taken where coatings fail first, such as edges, welds and inside corners, not only on flat faces. For background on the methods themselves, see our guide to
ASTM standards for powder coating
, which explains each standard in plain terms for anyone checking powder coating QA.

A tape adhesion rating shows how firmly the coat is bonded to the metal, and quality assurance for powder coating relies on it more than any other single test. A low rating points straight back to prep, which is why we check the surface before any powder goes on.
Documents You Can Request

You can request a copy of our certificate, third-party test reports and an inspection report for your order. Together they give your quality team the quality documentation it needs without chasing us for details after delivery.

Many customers ask for these papers during procurement audits or before adding a new coater to an approved supplier list. Tell us what your system requires, whether that is readings per part, per batch or a summary, and we will match it. Records are kept against each job, so documents for an earlier order can be pulled later for your own quality assurance file. This is the practical side of powder coating quality assurance.
Why Certified Quality Matters to Buyers

Certified powder coating quality assurance lowers your risk. It shows that prep, coating and inspection follow written steps, so finishes stay consistent between orders and any problem can be traced back to a stage and a date.

For manufacturers and contractors, that consistency protects warranties and keeps parts out of rework. For public buyers, it supports tender requirements. The same standard applies whether we coat a single bracket or a large frame, as our
large part powder coating
page shows, and it covers the prep done by our
sandblasting services
. Our quality guarantee rests on that quality assurance system, not on promises.
How Long Checks Take

Inspection is built into our standard 48 hour turnaround, so certified checks do not slow an order down. Extra testing, such as outside-lab corrosion exposure, adds time, and we confirm that schedule before work begins.
Copies of the certificate and standard reports are usually sent with the order or soon after. Planning ahead for quality assurance paperwork keeps your own approvals moving.

Short answer: yes, you can see the proof behind our quality claims. These answers cover the certifying body, reports and failed checks, and they appear only on this page, written for buyers and auditors.

body.text: Koojo Custom Powder Coating | Last updated 23 October 2026

children.text: Who We Are

Koojo Custom Powder Coating is a powder coating shop at 10874 Steeles Ave E, Milton, ON L9T 2X8, serving customers across the Greater Toronto Area since 2012. We are responsible for the personal information we collect, and we handle it in line with Canada’s Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA).
Information We Collect
We collect only what we need to answer you and quote your project. When you use our Get a Quote form, call us or send an email, that can include:
Contact details: your name, email address and phone number.
Project details: the message you send, including part descriptions, sizes, quantities and any photos or drawings you choose to share.
Technical data: basic information such as browser type, device and pages visited, collected through our website platform as described under Cookies.
Please do not send us sensitive personal information, such as financial account or government ID numbers. We do not need it to quote or coat your parts.
How We Use Your Information
We use your information to respond to enquiries and provide quotes, and for the purposes below:
Communicate with you about your project, timing, pickup and delivery.
Keep business and job records and meet our legal and tax obligations.
Improve our customer service and the way our website works.
We do not send marketing emails without your consent, and we will never use your information for a purpose you would not reasonably expect.
Who We Share It With
We do not sell or rent your personal information, and we do not share it with third parties except where this is needed to fulfil your request or is required by law.

Service providers that help us run the business, such as our website platform (Wix) and our email provider, may handle information on our behalf. They may store or process it outside Canada, including in the United States, where it can be accessed by courts and authorities under local law. We ask these providers to protect it appropriately.
Cookies and Website Analytics

Our website is built on Wix, which uses cookies and similar technologies to load pages securely and keep the site working. We may also use basic analytics to see how many people visit and which pages they read. You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings, although some parts of the site may not work as expected if you do.
How Long We Keep It and How We Protect It
We keep quote requests and job records only as long as needed to respond, complete your order and meet our business, tax and legal obligations, and then delete or anonymise them.

We use reasonable physical, technical and organisational safeguards, and we limit access to staff who need it. No method of transmission or storage over the internet is completely secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.
Your Choices and Rights

You can ask to see the personal information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or withdraw your consent to our using it, subject to legal and contractual limits. Email sales@koojopowdercoating.com or call (905) 876-7060, and we will reply within 30 days.
If you are not satisfied with our response, you can contact the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada at priv.gc.ca.
Other Websites, Children and Changes to This Policy
Our site may link to other websites, such as Google Maps or our Google Business Profile. We do not control their privacy practices, so please read their policies.
Our website and services are intended for businesses and adults, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children.
We may update this policy from time to time. The date at the top of this page shows when it was last revised, and continued use of the site after an update means you accept the revised policy.
Contact Us About Privacy

Questions about this policy or your information? Contact Koojo Custom Powder Coating at 10874 Steeles Ave E, Milton, ON L9T 2X8. Phone (905) 876-7060, Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Email sales@koojopowdercoating.com. You can also use our
Contact Us
page or
request a quote

children.text: What Are Our Powder Coating Services?

They are ten connected metal finishing services that take a part from rust, scale or old paint to a cured, tested finish. Some jobs need one step, others need several, and we combine them into a single order.

Powder coating itself is a dry powder sprayed by electrostatic spray and hardened by oven curing, which gives protective coatings that resist chips, fading and corrosion better than many liquid paints. Around that core sit the supporting coating services: surface preparation, blasting, colour work, stripping and recoating, plus specialist work for vehicles, wheels, buildings, volume orders and one-off pieces. That one-stop finishing approach keeps quality consistent and saves you managing several suppliers, each with its own schedule, standards and paperwork.
What We Can Coat: Size, Weight and Volume

Parts as long as 23 ft and as heavy as 6,000 lb fit our line, in quantities from a single piece to recurring batches. Metals include carbon steel and aluminum, structural steel, cast iron and galvanized steel.

content.text: In-house, plus mobile sandblasting on site

children.text: Our service range is planned around size from the first call, so long frames and heavy bases get their own cure cycle. We handle one-off and production work on the same line, and batches of small parts can share an oven load with a larger piece in the same colour. For full limits and a fit check, see
large part powder coating
, which explains how big work is loaded and racked under our powder coating services.
How Our Powder Coating Services Work

Every order follows the same eight steps, from checking your drawing to packing the finished parts. The steps are fixed so results stay consistent, whether we handle one service for you or all of them.
Inspection & Spec Review

We check each part against your drawing, confirm the finish and mark every surface that must stay bare. We also agree which of our powder coating services the part needs, so nothing is added later without your approval.
Abrasive & Mobile Sandblasting
Blasting removes rust, mill scale and old coatings, in the shop or on site, leaving a clean profile the powder can grip.
Cleaning & Phosphate Pretreatment
Degreasing and pretreatment prepare the metal so the powder bonds firmly, then parts are rinsed and fully dried. Pretreatment also slows corrosion under the coating if the finish is ever damaged.
Masking & Plugging
Masking and plugging protect threads, mounting faces and contact points. Plugs and high-temperature tape come off after curing, leaving clean edges.
Electrostatic Powder Application
Charged powder wraps around edges and into corners for even coverage, the core of our service range. Film build is kept even so colour and gloss match across every part in a batch.
Oven Curing
Parts cure at 180–200 °C until the metal itself reaches temperature, so thick sections cure fully. Curing time follows the powder maker's data sheet, not guesswork.
Quality Inspection & DFT Check
Quality inspection covers film thickness, adhesion, colour and coverage before release. Results are recorded, so test reports can go out with any of our coating services on request.
Packaging & Shipping
Packaging and shipping protect finished faces, and the job ends with pickup or delivery. Finished faces are wrapped so they arrive exactly as they left inspection, the final step of every service.

Powder gives durable finishes in almost any colour, wet paint suits quick touch-ups and heat-sensitive parts, and galvanizing gives zinc protection with limited looks. The table compares all three at a glance.

children.text: Powder Coating by Industry at a Glance
This table summarizes how finish needs change from one sector to the next.
How We Match a Finish to Your Sector

We match a finish to your sector in four steps: review, prepare, apply and cure, then inspect. Because powder coating by industry depends on how each part is used, every step is adjusted to the sector instead of following one fixed recipe.

Review. We ask where the part will be used, how it is cleaned and which surfaces must stay bare. Photos, drawings and part counts help us give an accurate plan. Early review prevents rework and surprise costs.

Prepare. Pretreatment before coating drives adhesion and corrosion protection for steel. Depending on the metal, we degrease, treat, remove rust, then finish with careful masking. Skipping this stage is the most common reason coatings fail early.
Apply and cure. Electrostatic powder application wraps thermoset powder evenly around the part, which then enters the curing oven at roughly 180–200 °C. Our load capacity is up to 6,000 lb; see
capabilities
. Heavy parts need longer oven time to reach temperature all the way through.
Inspect. We check coverage, appearance and film thickness before release, then pack parts to protect the finish. Any part that misses the standard is corrected before release.

Quality and Certification

children.text: What Is Industrial Powder Coating?

Industrial powder coating is a dry, electrostatically applied thermoset finish, cured at roughly 180 to 200 °C and engineered for parts in heavy service rather than for appearance alone. Compared with decorative work, it demands tighter control of surface profile, film thickness and cure, backed by documented testing.

An industrial coating system is chosen for the exposure the part will face: indoor plant floors, washdown areas, outdoor yards or salted roads. That choice sets the blast grade, pretreatment, powder chemistry and whether a primer is needed. Typical parts include machine bases, conveyor frames, structural beams, storage racks, electrical enclosures, safety guards, hoppers, chutes and trailer components. New to the finish itself? Start with our guide on what is powder coating, then come back here for the industrial detail that matters on spec work.
What We Can Coat: Size, Weight & Volume

We coat parts from small brackets to structural assemblies weighing up to 6,000 lb, as single pieces or recurring production batches. Our cure oven fits [confirm oven size], so most frames, bases and long beams are coated whole rather than cut into sections.

content.text: Carbon steel, structural steel, aluminum, galvanized steel, cast iron
One-off parts to recurring production runs
[Confirm typical parts per day or week]

children.text: Coating large weldments whole avoids extra joints and touch-up lines in the finished industrial powder coating. Every heavy-duty powder coating job is scheduled so cure time is never rushed. Full equipment limits are listed on our large part powder coating page.
Our Industrial Powder Coating Process

Every order moves through the same eight controlled steps, from spec review to packed shipment, so results repeat from the first part to the last. Each step is recorded against your drawing, which is how we meet an industrial coating spec rather than simply a colour.
Inspection & Spec Review

We check the drawing or spec sheet, metal type, weld quality, part weight and exposure environment, then confirm the powder, colour, film build and any test requirements in writing before work starts.
Abrasive & Mobile Sandblasting

Rust, mill scale and old coatings are removed by abrasive blasting, leaving a clean, angular profile that meets your specified SSPC or ISO blast grade. Fixed or oversized structures can be blasted on site with our sandblasting services.
Cleaning & Phosphate Pretreatment

Parts are degreased, rinsed and treated with iron or zinc phosphate to improve adhesion and slow under-film corrosion. Our powder coating surface preparation page explains each chemical stage in more detail.
Masking & Plugging
Threads, bores, bearing seats, grounding points and mating faces are plugged or taped with high-temperature masking, so they stay bare and fit correctly at assembly.
Electrostatic Powder Application

Charged powder is sprayed onto the grounded part, wrapping edges and recesses evenly. Primer and topcoat are applied in sequence when a two-coat industrial powder coating system is specified for harsher exposure.
Oven Curing

Parts are cured to the powder maker's schedule, typically 180 to 200 °C for 10 to 20 minutes at metal temperature, so the film fully cross-links. Thick, heavy sections are given longer soak time to reach temperature.
Quality Inspection & DFT Check
We measure dry film thickness, run adhesion checks and inspect colour, gloss and coverage on each batch. Readings are recorded for every batch and can be supplied with your order.
Packaging & Shipping
Finished parts are wrapped, blocked and strapped to protect the powder-coated surface in transit, then shipped or held for pickup at our shop.
Which Powder Is Best for Industrial Parts?

The right powder depends on exposure. Epoxy suits indoor and chemical exposure, polyester suits outdoor UV, and a zinc-rich primer under a topcoat suits road salt and high corrosion. Matching chemistry to exposure is the core of heavy-duty powder coating.

Performance Testing & Quality Control

We verify each order against measurable, repeatable tests, not appearance alone. Film thickness and adhesion are checked in our shop on every batch, while salt spray and corrosivity ratings are matched to the powder supplier's certified data for your environment.

This documentation is what separates industrial powder coating from cosmetic work, and it is available on every powder-coated order. Our ASTM standards for powder coating guide explains each method, and our powder coating quality assurance page covers certification.
Industries & Parts We Coat

Our industrial coating customers range from fabricators and OEMs to contractors and municipalities. Most send steel parts that work hard: frames, bases, guards, chutes, bollards and implements, each given industrial powder coating suited to its sector.
Metal Fabricators & Welding Shops: weldments and frames coated to spec. See powder coating for metal fabricators.
Manufacturing & Automation: conveyor frames, robotic bases and machine guards. See powder coating for manufacturers.
Machine Shops: precision-masked parts with clean threads. See powder coating for machine shops.
Contractors & Construction: structural steel, stairs and railings. See powder coating for contractors.
Food Processing Equipment: washdown-resistant line frames. See powder coating for food processing equipment.
Agricultural & Heavy Equipment: implements and trailers. See agricultural equipment powder coating.
Municipal & Institutional: bollards and public metalwork. See powder coating for municipalities.
Industrial Powder Coating vs Wet Paint vs Galvanizing

Powder coating gives the toughest chip-resistant colour finish, galvanizing gives sacrificial zinc protection, and wet paint is easiest to apply on site. For outdoor steel, galvanizing under a powder-coated topcoat often performs best.
For full comparisons, see powder coating vs wet paint and powder coating vs galvanizing.

What Affects Cost and Lead Time
Price and lead time depend on part size and weight, surface condition, masking, powder type, number of coats and order volume. Clean, bare steel in a standard colour moves fastest.
Size and weight: larger parts use more oven space and handling.
Surface condition: rust, mill scale or old paint add blasting.
Masking: every plugged hole adds labour.
Coats: primers and two-coat systems add cure cycles.
Volume: repeat runs in one colour cost less per part.

data.title: Powder Coating Surface Preparation & Pretreatment
data.summary: Powder coating surface preparation is the cleaning, pretreatment and masking work that decides whether a powder finish bonds for years or fails within months. At Koojo Custom Powder Coating, every part is degreased, chemically treated, rinsed and dried before any powder goes on. Since 2012, our Milton team has prepared more than 10,000 items for fabricators, manufacturers and contractors across the GTA, with a 48-hour turnaround. Whether you send raw steel weldments, machined components or aluminum brackets, our surface preparation for powder coating removes oil, residue and contamination so the coating can grip the metal. Request a quote below, or call (905) 876-7060, Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, and our team will advise on the right pretreatment for your parts.

$media.alt: A coated plate with masking still in place

content.text: By the Koojo Custom Powder Coating production team | Updated 14 October 2026
Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | 48 Hr Turnaround | Google Rating

children.text: What Is Powder Coating Surface Preparation?

Powder coating surface preparation is the sequence of cleaning, chemical treatment, masking and drying steps that readies bare metal for powder. It removes oils, oxides and soils, then leaves a clean, slightly reactive surface so the powder bonds firmly while it cures.

Powder cannot hide a dirty surface. Thermoset powder melts and flows in the oven at a cure temperature of 180–200 °C, so any film of cutting oil, forming lubricant or fingerprint residue trapped underneath causes craters, fisheyes and weak powder coating adhesion. Proper powder coating pretreatment solves two problems at once: it cleans the part, and it adds a thin conversion coating that improves grip and slows rust under the finish.

Without it, even premium powder can lift at edges and welds. That is why we treat surface preparation for powder coating as a core production step, never a cosmetic extra, and why every job at our shop begins here rather than in the spray booth. The powder is the visible finish, but the bond underneath decides how long it stays attached.
How Does Our Powder Coating Pretreatment Process Work?

Our powder coating surface preparation has five stages: inspection and masking, alkaline cleaning, rinse, phosphate conversion treatment, and a final rinse and dry-off. Each stage removes one specific barrier to adhesion, and parts move to coating only when they are clean, dry and free of flash rust.

Inspection and masking (on arrival). We check each part for heavy rust, old coatings, weld spatter and trapped oil. We then mask threads, bores and contact faces with high-temperature plugs and tape. Masking for powder coating protects precision features, so bolts still thread in after curing.

Alkaline cleaning. A cleaning bath performs oil and grease removal from cutting fluid, shop dirt and handling marks. Degreasing before powder coating is the strongest defence against craters, so we never skip it, even on parts that look clean.
Rinse. Clean water flushes cleaner residue, which would otherwise interfere with the chemical treatment that follows.

Phosphate pretreatment. This step forms a thin crystalline layer on the metal. The layer improves grip and gives the finish a protected base. Metal pretreatment for powder coating always depends on the substrate and on where the finished part will live.
Final rinse and dry-off. A last rinse removes chemical salts. The rinse and dry-off step then drives off moisture, which is the key to flash rust prevention. Parts go straight to coating once dry.

Timing matters as much as chemistry. Every stage sits inside our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Because multi-stage pretreatment happens first, coating and curing always start from a controlled surface. Our powder coating pretreatment is built into the schedule, not added afterwards, so a well-prepared part never waits on a separate booking. If your project has a deadline, tell us when you request a quote and we will plan around it. Clear communication at the start keeps powder coating surface preparation on schedule and avoids surprises at pickup.
Which Metals and Parts Need Surface Preparation for Powder Coating?

Every metal needs preparation, but the method changes with the substrate. Steel needs oil and residue removed, aluminum needs its oxide layer controlled, and galvanized steel needs careful treatment and outgassing management. Fabricated and machined parts also need masking before coating.
Steel. Steel pretreatment targets mill oil, weld residue removal and early rust. It is the most common job we handle, and the metal pretreatment for powder coating we apply is matched to the part.

Aluminum. Aluminum pretreatment uses a chemical treatment that cleans the surface and builds a bonding layer, because raw aluminum oxidizes quickly. Here, the chemical treatment protects adhesion more than any other step.
Galvanized steel. Zinc surfaces respond differently from bare steel and can release trapped gases while curing, so galvanized parts get their own preparation plan.

Typical parts include welded frames, brackets, guards, railings, bollards, machine components and equipment housings. Each one needs powder coating surface preparation sized to its shape, because deep corners and enclosed sections trap oil and moisture more easily than flat plate. Our fabricated parts pretreatment and custom part preparation cover one-off pieces and repeat production runs, with the same standard applied to both. Good preparation means each load leaves with a production-ready surface, whatever the shape or size.
What Pretreatment Options Does Koojo Offer?

Koojo matches the pretreatment to the part. Most steel receives a standard wash and phosphate sequence, aluminum and galvanized metal get a suitable chemical pretreatment, and parts with threads or sealing faces receive detailed masking. Heavy rust or old coatings are handled before pretreatment.
Standard pretreatment wash stages. Cleaning, rinsing, conversion treatment and drying for everyday steel parts, delivered as consistent powder coating pretreatment.

Iron or zinc phosphate. Iron phosphate pretreatment suits many indoor and general-duty parts. Zinc phosphate pretreatment is considered when a part needs extra rust prevention before coating, such as outdoor equipment.
Plugging and masking. Threaded hole masking, bore plugs and tape protect dimensions. Tell us about special requirements when you quote.
Heavy cleaning first. Thick rust, scale or an old finish needs more than a wash. Our
sandblasting service
removes it mechanically, and our
restoration and recoating service
handles aged coatings, before pretreatment begins.

Not sure which option fits? Send photos and the part material. We will recommend an approach, and our surface preparation for powder coating advice comes with your quote. Choosing the right powder coating surface preparation up front is far cheaper than fixing a failed finish later, and for aluminum and galvanized work we select the metal pretreatment for powder coating that suits that substrate.
How Do We Check Pretreatment Quality?

We verify preparation through visual inspection, surface checks and adhesion testing on the finished coating. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, our inspection steps are documented, and test reports are available on request, so you can trust the work behind every finish.

Pretreatment quality control starts before the bath: we look for oil, rust and weld residue on arrival. After rinsing, a clean surface should hold a continuous film of water, which is the idea behind the water break test. On the finished part, a cross-hatch adhesion test to ASTM D3359 shows whether the powder is gripping the metal.

Surface contamination is the most common cause of coating adhesion failure, and it shows up later as peeling and blistering. Catching it early costs far less than recoating. Strong powder coating pretreatment also keeps results consistent from batch to batch, and the same surface preparation for powder coating standard applies to every load. We hold our metal pretreatment for powder coating to the same documented checks, and powder coating surface preparation is never signed off until the part passes them. For the blasting cleanliness grades behind these checks, read our guide to
surface preparation standards
, and see our
certification
page for details on how we work. Our metal cleaning before powder coating is part of that documented process.
See Surface Preparation in a Real Project

Welded frames arrive with weld residue, forming oil and tight tolerances, which makes powder coating surface preparation critical. Our conveyor frame case study shows what a documented job looks like for a real production customer, from the incoming part to the finished coating.
Read the
conveyor frame for an automotive plant

project to see the part, metal, size, powder, colour code and turnaround recorded for a real production job. Before and after photos show the standard we hold ourselves to, and the same documented approach applies to your parts.
Which Industries Rely on Our Surface Preparation?

Fabricators, machine shops, manufacturers and contractors rely on us most. These customers need dependable industrial metal cleaning, tight masking and repeatable results that match the next batch. Our approach scales from single parts to production runs, and every customer receives the same careful treatment.
See how we support
metal fabricators and welding shops
, where weld residue is the main concern, and
machine shops
, where masking protects precision features. Our powder coating surface preparation also supports our wider
industrial powder coating
work, our metal pretreatment for powder coating on large fabrications, and the full range of
powder coating services
at our Milton shop.

Short answer: preparation is the cleaning, treatment and masking that comes before powder, and it controls how long the finish lasts. These answers cover failure risks, phosphate choices, masking limits and timing, so you know what to expect before you drop off parts.

items.question: What happens if powder coating surface preparation is skipped?

children.text: Oil and residue stay under the powder, so the finish can crater, peel or blister, and rust can creep in from edges. Skipping surface preparation for powder coating usually means early failure and a costly strip and redo.

items.question: What is the difference between iron and zinc phosphate?

children.text: Iron phosphate forms a light conversion layer and suits general-duty indoor parts, while the right metal pretreatment for powder coating on outdoor equipment is often zinc. Zinc phosphate forms a heavier crystalline layer that offers stronger rust resistance for demanding or outdoor service.

items.question: Can you mask threads and holes?

content.text: By the Koojo Custom Powder Coating production team | Updated 14 October 2026
Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | 48 Hr Turnaround | Google Rating

children.text: What Are Sandblasting Services?

Sandblasting services use compressed air to drive abrasive media against metal, removing rust, scale and old surface debris. The result is clean, bare metal with an even texture that lets powder coating grip firmly and last for years, even in tough outdoor conditions.

The word sandblasting is common, but most modern work uses other abrasives, so the broader names are media blasting and abrasive blasting. Each media cuts differently. Aluminum oxide blasting and steel grit blasting cut fast and leave a rougher surface, while glass bead blasting leaves a smoother, cleaner finish. The texture left behind is called the surface profile, or anchor profile, and it gives powder something to hold. Good blast cleaning removes everything that would stop a coating from bonding and leaves a bare metal finish ready to coat.

That is why we treat industrial sandblasting as part of the coating process, not a separate chore. Sandblasting and powder coating work best when one team plans both, because clean steel starts to show flash rust soon after blasting. Skipping this link in the chain is the most common reason a coating fails early.
How Does Our Sandblasting Process Work?

Our sandblasting services follow five stages: inspection, blast media selection, blasting, cleanup, and handoff to coating. Each stage protects the metal and the finish, and blasted parts move to coating quickly so rust never gets a chance to return to the metal before the coating goes on.

Inspection and planning (on arrival). We check each part for heavy rust, pitted and scaled steel, weld spatter and thin sections. We then decide whether the job suits our shop or on-site sandblasting. Early inspection lets us flag problem areas before they cost you time.

Blast media selection. The right media depends on the metal and the finish you need. Tough rust and scale call for harder media, while softer metals and cosmetic parts need gentler options. We confirm the choice with you when the finish or tolerance is critical.

Blasting. Our operators work across every surface, including welds, corners and recesses. They adjust pressure and distance so rust and mill-scale removal is complete without damaging thin sections. Industrial sandblasting at this stage is methodical, never rushed.
Cleanup. Compressed air and brushing clear spent media and dust from holes, seams and enclosed sections. Trapped grit would cause defects under the powder, so we never skip this step.
Inspection and handoff. We confirm a uniform, blast-cleaned surface, then move the part toward coating as soon as possible, since flash rust can form quickly on clean steel.

Timing matters as much as technique. Shop blasting sits inside our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. For mobile sandblasting, tell us the site, access and schedule when you request a quote and we will plan the visit around your deadline. Industrial sandblasting is scheduled alongside coating, so a blasted part never waits long between steps. That planning prevents the gaps that let bare metal rust, and it keeps your project moving.
Which Metals and Parts Need Sandblasting?

Steel and iron benefit most, because rust and scale form naturally on them. Cast parts, structural steel, fabricated frames and heavy equipment also respond well. Thin or soft metals need gentler media, so our sandblasting services plan the method for each metal before blasting starts.

Steel and iron. Sandblasting steel removes rust and mill scale, the hard grey layer left by hot rolling that blocks coating adhesion. It is the most common job we handle, and it suits everything from small brackets to large frames.
Welded and cast parts. Sandblasting weldments cleans weld discoloration and spatter, and gives rust removal from metal even in tight corners.
Aluminum and softer metals. Gentler media protects the surface, so we choose finer abrasives and lower pressure for these parts, which keeps edges and details sharp.

Typical work includes sandblasting structural steel, sandblasting gates and railings, sandblasting trailers and frames, machine bases and equipment housings. Sandblasting heavy equipment and sandblasting large fabrications can be done in our shop or on site, so confirm the part size when you request a quote. Whether you need sandblasting metal parts one at a time or industrial sandblasting for a full production run, we plan the abrasive blasting to protect the metal.
What Sandblasting Options Does Koojo Offer?

Koojo offers shop blasting for parts we can move, a mobile service for work on site, and a choice of blast media to suit the metal. Blasting is most often paired with powder coating, so ask us how your job should be planned from start to finish.
Shop sandblasting. Parts come to our Milton shop, where blasting happens in a controlled setting with dust containment and a fast route into coating.

Mobile sandblasting. Our mobile blasting crew brings on-site blasting equipment to structures, large frames and fixed equipment that are hard to move. Portable sandblasting equipment suits these jobs. Share site access and layout when you quote.
Media choices. Blast media selection covers aluminum oxide, steel grit and glass bead, matched to the metal and the finish you want. Larger industrial sandblasting jobs often use a mix of media.
What comes next. After blasting, many parts still need washing and masking, which our
powder coating surface preparation
service covers. Parts with aged coatings may suit our
restoration and recoating
service.

Not sure which option fits? Send photos and the part material. We will recommend an approach, and our sandblasting services advice comes with your quote. Choosing the right method up front avoids a damaged part, and protects the rust protection your coating is meant to provide.
How Do We Check Blasting Quality?

We verify blasting through visual inspection and a surface check before coating. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, our inspection steps are documented, and test reports are available on request, so you can trust the work behind every finish.

Quality starts at intake, when we look for heavy rust, thick scale and old coatings. After blasting, a blast-cleaned surface should look even in colour, with no shiny rust patches, leftover scale or traces of old paint. Surface profile matters too. If the surface is too smooth, powder grips poorly, and if it is too rough, peaks can show through the finish and shorten its life. We check this before parts move on, and we flag any concern with you early.

Our sandblasting services are never signed off until the part passes these checks. Consistent industrial sandblasting also means the next batch matches the last, because we keep records that support repeat orders. Cleanup is part of quality. Loose grit left in seams spoils the coating, so we clear it before parts move on. Because clean bare steel can show flash rust quickly, we plan coating soon after blasting, and we hold shop and mobile work to the same documented checks every time. See our
certification
page for details on how we work. Careful abrasive blasting also leaves the clean bare steel that strong coatings need.
See Sandblasting in a Real Project

Outdoor metalwork such as bollards and gates collects rust, scale and old coatings, which makes sandblasting services a smart first step. Our safety bollards case study documents the part, metal, size, powder, colour code and turnaround for a real customer, so you can see what a documented job looks like.
Read the
safety bollards

project to see the finished result. Before and after photos show the standard we hold ourselves to, from the bare metal stage through to the finished coating, and the same documented approach applies to your parts.
Which Industries Use Our Sandblasting Services?

Fabricators, contractors, farm and heavy equipment owners and manufacturers use us most. These customers need dependable industrial sandblasting, quick turnaround and a clean surface that supports coating. Our approach scales from single parts to production runs, with the same care every time.
See how we support
contractors and construction
teams, who often need work done on site, and
agricultural and heavy equipment
owners, where heavy rust is the main concern, so you can find the page that matches your work. Our sandblasting services also support our wider
industrial powder coating
work and the full range of
powder coating services
at our Milton shop.

children.text: What Are Custom Powder Coating Colours?

Custom powder coating colours are shades matched to your specification rather than picked from a stock range. The powder is sprayed on electrostatically and cured in an oven, so the colour becomes part of a hard, even finish instead of a thin layer of paint.

Most requests fall into three groups. The first is a standard shade from our powder colour range. The second is RAL colour matching, where you give us a RAL number. The third is a colour match to a sample, where you send us a chip, swatch or small part. Each group changes how we source the powder and how we confirm the result with you. A custom powder coat colour is only as good as its reference, so a clear specification saves time.

Custom powder coat colour is only half of the decision. Sheen levels decide how that colour looks once it is on the part. Gloss powder coating is smooth and bright, matte powder coating cuts glare, and satin powder coating sits in between. The same shade can read very differently in each, so we talk through sheen before we order the powder.
How We Match and Apply Custom Powder Coating Colours

We confirm your colour reference, prepare the metal, apply the powder electrostatically, cure it at 180–200 °C and inspect the result against your sample. Each step protects the colour match and the finish quality from the first brief to the final check.

Colour brief. Send a RAL number, a RAL colour chart reference, a brand specification or physical colour samples. Samples are best, because screens and printed charts rarely show the true shade. This is where custom colour matching starts.
Powder selection. We check the powder coating colour chart and our supplier range for your shade and finish. If a colour must be ordered in, we confirm the timing with you before work starts.
Surface preparation. Clean metal holds colour evenly. We degrease, remove rust and scale, and pretreat the part where needed, as described on our
surface preparation
page.
Masking. We plug threads and bores and cover contact points so your custom powder coat colour stays only where you want it.
Spray and cure. The powder is applied electrostatically, then cured in the oven at 180–200 °C. The heat melts the powder and bonds the pigment into one continuous film.
Inspection. We compare the finished custom powder coating colours with your reference, check coverage and thickness, and look for defects before packing.

Some finishes need an extra step. Candy colours and certain effect powders are often built as a two-coat finish, with a coloured base followed by a second layer. This adds time, so we explain it when we quote. For repeat orders, we record the powder and colour code to support batch colour consistency on later runs of your custom powder coating colours. Whether your custom powder coating colours are in stock changes the timing, so we check availability early.
Which Parts and Metals Can We Colour?
We apply custom powder coating colours to steel and aluminum parts, from small brackets to large fabricated frames. The part must withstand oven curing, so we review each item before quoting. See our
capabilities
page for size and weight limits.

Typical work includes railings, gates, bollards, machine guards, equipment housings and frames. Powder coating for fabricated parts is a large share of what we do, and one consistent colour across welded assemblies is often the main requirement. Galvanized and cast metals can need extra checks because trapped gases may affect the surface, so tell us the material when you ask for a quote. Send photos with your request so we can check size, weight and masking needs early. Every custom powder coat colour we apply is matched to the metal as well as the specification.

Parts that live outdoors also need the right powder. UV-resistant powder coating holds its colour better in sunlight, which matters for fences, outdoor furniture and building metalwork. For an outdoor-durable finish on exterior products, see our
architectural powder coating
service, or read our guide to
outdoor furniture finishes
Finish Options for Your Colour Choice

You can pair any custom powder coat colour with a finish type: gloss, satin, matte, textured, metallic, candy or clear coat. The finish changes how the colour looks, feels and wears, so it is worth choosing both together. These powder coating finishes give you plenty of room to match a design.
Gloss and high-gloss finish. A smooth, reflective surface that is easy to wipe clean.
Satin and low-gloss finish. A softer sheen that shows fewer fingerprints and marks.
Matte. A flat, modern look with the least glare.
Textured powder coating. A wrinkle finish or hammertone finish adds pattern, and an anti-slip textured finish improves grip. Texture also hides surface imperfections such as light weld marks.
Metallic powder coat. Our custom colour powder coating can include silver, bronze and copper metallics that add depth and sparkle.
Candy powder coating. A translucent custom powder coat colour over a base that gives rich colour depth.
Clear coat powder coating. A transparent top layer that protects metallic and candy effects.
Choosing between metallic shades? Our
metallic finishes guide
explains the differences, and our
RAL colour guide
shows how RAL numbers translate to powder.
How We Check Colour and Finish Quality
We check your custom powder coat colour against your reference, measure film thickness and test adhesion before parts leave the shop. Our quality steps are outlined on our
certification
page, and test reports are available on request. Ask us about them when your project specification requires proof.

Where a job calls for it, test methods include ASTM D3359 for adhesion, ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance. Our certification is held through the Absolute Bureau of Certification. A custom powder coating colour is only useful if it stays attached and even, so we test the finish as well as the shade.
Fade resistance depends on the powder chemistry and the pigment. Bright reds and oranges fade faster outdoors than neutral tones, so we ask where the part will be used before recommending a powder.
Colour Work in Practice
Our
safety bollards
project shows how a durable colour is chosen for exposed steel. The case study lists the part, metal, powder, colour code and turnaround, so you can see how the finish was specified.
You can also browse more finished parts on our
Our Work

page, filtered by industrial, automotive, architectural and specialty projects. A good colour brief includes the part, the metal, the colour reference and the finish. With those four details, we can quote custom powder coating colours accurately and confirm the match before curing.
Who Uses Custom Colour Finishes

Fabricators, welding shops, contractors and manufacturers order custom powder coating colours most often, because their parts must match a client's brand or a building's design. Consistent custom powder coating colours matter as much as the shade itself.
Metal fabricators and welding shops
send us weldments that must match a customer's colour.
Contractors and construction

teams order railings, gates and site metalwork in colours chosen by designers. Branded colour matching and corporate colour finishes are common for equipment makers. For larger production runs, see our
industrial powder coating
service, or browse all of our
powder coating services

data.summary: Powder coat stripping and recoating removes a failed, damaged or unwanted finish and replaces it with a fresh powder coat finish that bonds to clean metal. Whether your railings are peeling, your frames are chipped or your equipment has rusted, our powder coat removal and recoating service restores the metal and its protection. $media.alt: Spraying a steel frame in the booth

content.text: By the Koojo Custom Powder Coating production team | Updated 14 October 2026

children.text: Our standard turnaround is 48 hours for typical shop orders, and we are open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Heavily rusted or multi-part jobs are scheduled when we quote, once we know the size, the condition and how much old coating removal the parts need.
